bearings.paper_claim: Table A1 gives Senate-insider and APSA-Fellow mean Big Five ratings for 129 senators, feeding main-paper Tables 2-5. Table A2 gives academic ratings for 126 senator name entries (text count), used only in main-paper Table 1. Each row carries a rating count. Observed values run 1.00-7.00 with 0.50 increments noted by the authors.
bearings.paper_location: Appendix p.1 front note; Table A1 (pp.2-4) and note; Table A2 (pp.5-7) and note
bearings.system_side: build_big5_senate_gold.py writes a SHA-256-pinned frozen artifact (data/stance/big5_senate_expert_gold.json) keeping panel, source name, page and ratings_n. EXPECTED_COUNTS is 129 insiders and 125 academics (line 20); the 1-7 range check is at line 62. The artifact has 129 insider and 125 academic records. The academic count is one short of the 126 text entries: the academic Feingold row (malformed cell 4..33, text line 1297) is absent; Feingold appears only as an insider with ratings_n 2. The except branch at lines 56-61 drops that row silently, and its comment that only headings reach it is wrong. The usage contract at lines 85-90 is as stated. Both validators score per panel via map_gold.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Senate-only and historic; era unstated. Validates rank order on overlap with current members only, as the code caveat at b5_external_gold_validate.py:209 says. Ratings are as coded by the raters, not self-report.
bearings.verifier_note: Counts verified from text (129 and 126 name entries) and from the artifact (129 and 125). Value minimum corrected: observed minimum is 1.00, not 1.50. Scale anchors and aggregation rule absent from the appendix (searched). The 1-7 scale is asserted by the code, not stated by the authors.

bearings.paper_claim: Senators rated by only one coder are excluded from all analyses in the main paper but still appear in both tables. Bold and italic top and bottom designations apply only to senators with at least two coders.
bearings.paper_location: Table A1 note (appendix p.4, text lines 950-953); Table A2 note (text lines 1864-1869)
bearings.system_side: The primary validators do not filter on ratings_n. averaged_gold (b5_gold_multitrait_validate.py:83-97) averages insider and academic values with no count weight. oof_variant (126-134) keeps any row with a non-null trait. row_correlations (b5_external_gold_validate.py:114-118) filters only on null traits. Side probes respect the rule: b5_gold_criterion_probes.py:58-68 stratifies insider k=1 vs k>=2, and b5_o_weighted_look.py:399 weights by sqrt(ratings_n) with a k>=2 subset at line 417.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Same data and same inclusion rule. The size of the effect depends on how many current-roster matches are k=1 insiders, which was not counted here. Any k>=2 re-run is a new look under single-look discipline, not a free re-score.
bearings.verifier_note: Both table notes confirmed against the text. All cited code lines confirmed: no ratings_n filter in the primary validators, and the stratified and weighted probes exist as described.

bearings.paper_claim: The extremes of both panels are party-skewed. Democrats are 62% of the insider highest scorers and 65% of the lowest (main-paper Table 3, as cited). In the academic table 80% of high scores go to Democrats (Angus King counted as Democrat) and 80% of low scores to Republicans. The note calls the academic table A3; it is labelled A2.
bearings.paper_location: Appendix p.1 front note, text lines 11-17
bearings.system_side: The panel pass/miss pattern matches the artifact big5_gold_anchored.json: E and A pass both panels; O passes academics only (insider one-sided permutation p 0.104); N passes insiders only (academic p 0.195). Neither primary validator controls for party: b5_gold_multitrait_validate.py and b5_external_gold_validate.py contain no party term. The ONC look partials out female and republican covariates (b5_onc_dual_panel_look.py:121-164, covariates at 151-153, loader at 188). The claim that lexical O was reversed on a party check is not supported: the ONC candidate file marks O NOT_LOOKED_CRITERION_STOP_BAR_MISS, and no such result was found in the brain notes.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Party is a known fault line here. Panel-level correlations should be quoted with party strata or an UNSTRATIFIED label. The suggestion that O passes only against academics because of party is new agent analysis and stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062). The 62/65 and 80/80 figures describe only the extremes.
bearings.verifier_note: Percentages and the A2/A3 mislabel confirmed in the text. Table 3 figures are cited from the main paper and not checked. The O party-check reversal claim has no supporting artifact and is removed from system_side.

bearings.paper_claim: Insider, APSA Fellow and academic raters supply Big Five ratings of senators' public persona, usable as an external criterion for text-derived traits. The appendix calls these Big Five measures built from insider and academic data. It does not call them independent or observer ratings.
bearings.paper_location: Appendix p.1 front note; Tables A1-A2
bearings.system_side: The panels serve as external gold in b5_external_gold_validate.py and b5_gold_multitrait_validate.py. Full-sample gold-fitted weights are emitted after the OOF verdict (b5_gold_multitrait_validate.py:4-7, 136, 165). b5_profile_basis.py loads the gold artifact at line 128 and passes selected_weights into member_basis at lines 36-44, so for shipped composites the panels are no longer untouched; only the OOF figures are clean. The cited code does not refit the lexical instrument to RKH targets. The v2 lexical builder (big5_lexcal_v2.py docstring, lines 3-12) learns weights against behavioral criteria and describes the RKH and Mairesse weights as v1 priors.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies to senators who overlap the appendix and to text from the same public-persona era. Does not carry to House members or to genres (floor, interview, social) the raters never saw. Ratings describe perceived public persona, not self-report.
bearings.verifier_note: Gold-independence point confirmed in code. The RKH refit claim is not supported by the cited refs and is rewritten. The independent or observer wording is not in the appendix and is removed. Whether any other builder refits to RKH was not checked.

related.why: Item exists. Birkenmaier and Lechner 2025 is a text-based agency and communion measure; brain notes give prompting macro-F1 0.74-0.77. Paul highlighting codebook, Krippendorff alpha and macro-F1 is not found in the brain notes, so that part is unverified. Supplies a validation approach, not this appendix's criterion.

Item exists; ext describes Big Five measurement from floor speech text for US legislators, so the complement relation holds. Calling it the template for the lexical Big Five in Melange is not verified here.
Item exists; ext describes Big Five and LIWC relations across 52 categories. Using it as a realistic convergence ceiling for these panels is the analyst's inference, not the paper's claim.
Item exists; ext describes ideal and actual politician personality profiles, which supports the complement relation to observer-rated public-persona tables.

summary_issues: Value range wrong: the appendix minimum is 1.00 (e.g. the DeMint academic-table row region), not 1.50; maximum 7.00 is correct.

Academic row count: text has 126 senator name entries (insider 129 verified); the artifact has 125. Confirmed, not just agent-counted: the academic Feingold row with the malformed 4..33 cell (text line 1297) is absent from the artifact. The comment at build_big5_senate_gold.py:60 that only headings reach the except branch is wrong.
Claim that lexical O was reversed on the party check is unsupported by any artifact found (ONC candidate marks O NOT_LOOKED); remove.
Claim that the lexical Big Five is refit to RKH targets is not supported by the cited code; big5_lexcal_v2.py learns weights against behavioral criteria.

Paul alignment unverified: no mention of Mondak or Personality on the Hill found in brain notes beyond the gold-anchor entries, so the 'on disk only' listing and the stale-notes claim cannot be confirmed. Paul highlighting Birkenmaier codebook, Krippendorff alpha and macro-F1 is also unverified.
The gold-anchor pass/miss record (E and A both panels; O academic-only; N insider-only) is correctly reported and matches big5_gold_anchored.json.

Coverage: text file read via searches and counts; the PDF and page images were not available. All 129 insider and 126 academic name entries were counted from the text file. All four bearings and four related links were checked. paul_markup empty (no markup file). key_findings not present in the rel output, so none verified. Brain notes and research item files read only.
